items.headline: U.S. disables another ship trying to run Iran blockade
items.summary: U.S. Central Command said an aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman, disabling its propulsion without harming the crew. It is at least the 15th disclosed vessel the U.S. has disabled since the blockade of Iranian ports began.

items.headline: Zelenskyy calls Trump's 'friend' remark about Putin strange
items.summary: In a BBC interview, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged Washington to pressure Vladimir Putin and said of the Russian leader, "He can't be a friend." President Trump defended his comments, saying, "We want to make a deal. We want to stop the killing."

items.headline: Republicans signal openness to rethinking Trump's tariffs
items.summary: After midterm losses centered on rising costs, many congressional Republicans say they are open to reconsidering some tariffs, at least case by case. The shift follows the administration's proposal of new tariffs on China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other partners.

items.headline: Storm outages ease as East Coast begins cleanup
items.summary: More than 600,000 homes and businesses were still without power Friday morning, down from over 900,000 on Thursday, as heavy rain wound down. Crews carried out water rescues from New York to Virginia, including 39 people in Norfolk, and New York's Macy's parade was postponed to Saturday.

items.headline: Canada's top court upholds most of Quebec's religious-symbols ban
items.summary: Canada's Supreme Court upheld most of Quebec's 2019 Bill 21, which bars public employees in positions of authority, such as teachers and police, from wearing religious symbols. Prime Minister Mark Carney said he respected the ruling but his government would not use the constitutional override the law relies on.

items.headline: Mexico files complaint over DEA crime tip line
items.summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum filed a formal complaint with the U.S. Embassy over an anonymous DEA tip line, which her government calls foreign interference. Some Mexicans, including a Sinaloa journalist, have welcomed the line amid frustration over cartel violence.

items.headline: Russia's Kaliningrad emerges as a NATO flashpoint
items.summary: Moscow announced about 47 billion rubles for two railway ferries to supply its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad. Maritime incidents and rising tensions with NATO have made the territory a potential flashpoint.

items.headline: Thousands protest living costs in Puerto Rico
items.summary: About 30 groups organized a Black Friday protest in San Juan over record electricity rates, the cost of living and failing services. The new residential power rate of 33.86 cents per kilowatt-hour compares with a U.S. mainland average of 18.3 cents.

items.headline: Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape
items.summary: French film star Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault. The case is among the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence.

items.headline: Drones and a sniffer dog check on endangered orcas
items.summary: Scientists are using drones to collect whale breath and a detection dog to find stool samples to monitor the 76 remaining Southern Resident killer whales in the Salish Sea. Researchers say restoring salmon runs is the most important step, as the Chinook salmon the orcas eat have shrunk sharply in size.

digest.overview:
Thanksgiving storm outages fell from more than 900,000 customers Thursday to about 600,000 by Friday morning after water rescues from New York to Virginia. Many congressional Republicans said they are open to rethinking some of President Trump's tariffs after election losses driven by rising costs. Trump told U.S. service members that victory over Iran is "at hand." Thousands marched in San Juan, Puerto Rico, against record electricity rates and failing public services. Los Angeles schools quietly switched off Google's AI features on student devices. An official confirmed hackers breached the Air Force's cloud computing platform earlier this year.

Abroad, a U.S. aircraft disabled another blockade-running ship in the Gulf of Oman, and Kuwait formally protested to Iran over the drone strike that killed two Italians. Zelenskyy called Trump's description of Putin as a friend "strange," and EU leaders will retry a 45 billion-euro Ukraine loan at a Dec. 17–18 summit. Ukrainian intelligence said North Korea has paused military support for Russia, and Iran told Seoul that foreign forces in the Gulf raise tensions as South Korea plans to widen its naval unit's area. Russia is funding new rail ferries to Kaliningrad amid NATO tensions. Canada's Supreme Court largely upheld Quebec's ban on religious symbols for public servants, and Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum protested a DEA crime tip line. A French court ordered Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for rape and sexual assault, and Serbia's student movement nominated chemist Radomir Saicic for president. The U.N. warned hunger will worsen in 16 countries and regions, with Yemen, Somalia, Sudan and South Sudan most at risk.

home.overview:
Pittsburgh's defense scored twice in a 27–5 Black Friday rout of Denver, a final score never before seen in the NFL, as Mason Rudolph found DK Metcalf for a touchdown in the Steelers' first game since releasing Aaron Rodgers; the loss leaves the Broncos and Chiefs tied at 8-3 atop the AFC West. Brock Purdy, Justin Herbert and Drake Maye are all out Sunday, with DJ Uiagalelei set to start for the Chargers. NBA Cup group play ended with Miami knocking out the Knicks 108–105 behind Giannis Antetokounmpo's 22 points and 23 rebounds and San Antonio erasing a 20-point deficit to beat the Lakers 99–96; the Dec. 4–5 quarterfinals pair 76ers–Hawks, Spurs–Mavericks, Celtics–Pistons and Grizzlies–Trail Blazers. Baseball's labor deal expires Tuesday night.

Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3–2 on Morgan Gibbs-White's double, and Sunday brings Arsenal–Man City and the Merseyside derby, plus Dortmund–Leverkusen and Barcelona at Deportivo. Niclas Füllkrug's stoppage-time goal rescued a 3–3 draw for Werder Bremen against Gladbach, Brest beat Paris FC 1–0, and Southampton toppled Championship leaders Middlesbrough 2–0. In MLS, Columbus swept Inter Miami and Vancouver swept Real Salt Lake. K League 1 champions FC Seoul thrashed Daejeon 4–1. In the KBO, Kia's Kim Do-yeong became the youngest two-time MVP.

fact.answer:
Lightning heats the air in its path to as much as 50,000°F, so the air in the channel expands supersonically as a shock wave, then cools and contracts just as quickly. That sudden push is the sound we call thunder.

The rumble comes from the lightning's long, crooked path. Sound from the nearest part of the channel reaches you first, while sound from farther portions arrives later, stretching one flash into a rolling growl. A sharp crack or click means the lightning passed nearby; a rumble means it was at least several miles away.

To estimate distance, count the seconds between flash and thunder and divide by 5: five seconds is about a mile. Thunder carries only about 10 miles.
fact.question: Why does thunder rumble?
